grammarNotes: This lesson is about TIME. Let’s learn to TELL THE TIME in English? Let’s learn some vocabulary first, ok?
What time is it / What’s the time? = Que horas são?
a.m. = de madrugada e de manhã
p.m. = a partir de meio-dia até meia-noite
The common question to ask for the time is:
We use It is or It's to respond to the questions that ask for the time.
We use o'clock when there are NO minutes.
It’s eight. (not necessary to say o’clock)
There are two common ways of telling the time in English.
The DIGITAL time (hour + minutes) and the TRADITIONAL time (minutes + hour).
2) TRADITIONAL / ANALOGIC TIME – Say the minutes first and then the hour.  (Minutes + PAST / TO + Hour)
Antes da existência dos relógios digitais, se usavam os relógios analógicos.
There are 60 minutes in an hour.
For minutes 1-30 we use PAST or AFTER after the minutes.
For minutes 31-59 we use TO after the minutes.
So, it’s 5 after 3, it’s ten after 3, etc.
So, when it’s 7:15, we say it’s “quarter past seven”. Or when it’s 1:15, we say it’s “quarter after one”.
At minute 30, we say it’s “half past”.
So at 9:30, we would say it’s “half past nine” (or half an hour after 9:00).
At minute 45, we say it’s “quarter to” the next hour.
For example, at 5:45, we say it’s “quarter to six”
We don't normally use the 24-hour clock in English.
We use a.m. (am) for the morning and p.m. (pm) for the afternoon and evening.
a.m. is an abbreviation of the Latin phrase ante merīdiem meaning “before midday.”
P.m. is an abbreviation of post merīdiem, meaning “after midday.”
3am = Three o'clock in the morning. (não há uma palavra específica para “madrugada” em inglês)
For 12:00 there are four expressions in English.
Let’s practice! Now let’s do more exercises on the platform!

grammarNotes: Hello, guys! This is Book 1 Lesson 12 What time do you go to work? In this lesson you’ll learn about routines. The Bible character in this lesson is Daniel.
Let’s test your Bible knowledge. Answer these two questions.
Is Daniel’s story in the Old or in the New Testament?
Is Daniel a prophet? Yes or no?
Well, Daniel’s story is in the Old Testament and yes, he is a prophet!
Now read about Daniel’s routine and answers the questions.

I’m Daniel. I’m God’s prophet. I’m from Jerusalem, but I live in Babylon. I work for King Darius in his palace. I’m one of his administrators. I have three friends. Their names are: Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. Three times a day I get down to my knees. I pray and give thanks to God. Every day I go to work and when I come home, I pray and ask God for help.
Ok, now let’s learn some grammar.
Pause the video on the text. Underline the verbs in the text about Daniel. And the answers are:

I’m Daniel. I’m God’s prophet. I’m from Jerusalem, but I live in Babylon. I work for King Darius in his palace. I’m one of his administrators. I have three friends. Their names are: Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. Three times a day I get down to my knees. I pray and give thanks to God. Every day I go to work and when I come home, I pray and ask God for help.
These verbs are different than the verb TO BE. They are in the Simple Present. You use this verb tense to talk about routines, or habitual actions.
This is how you conjugate the verbs in the simple present.
Easy, huh? In the simple present, the verb has only two forms!
In the third person singular, you add -S, -ES, or -IES. Remember how you form the plural? That’s the same. Let’s review the rules?
Verbs ending in ss, sh, ch, x and o add es to form the third person singular:
I kiss, he kisses	I watch, he watches
When y follows a consonant, CONSONANT + Y, we change the y into i and add es:
When y follows a vowel, VOWEL + Y, we obey the usual rule:
Exception: verb to have - I have, you have, he, she, it has, we have, you have, they have
Now let’s do the exercises in the platform to consolidate this grammar topic.

lessons.title: Reading – Guessing the meaning of new words

grammarNotes: In this Reading exercise, let’s learn an important reading strategy - “guessing the meaning of new words”, ou seja, deduzir o significado das palavras em um texto. Esta dedução poderá ser tanto pelas palavras serem cognatas, por causa do contexto ou por causa do conhecimento prévio que você tenha do texto. Parte do seu aprendizado vai depender da sua habilidade de deduzir o que está sendo dito na língua em que você está aprendendo!
Vamos testar essa habilidade. Guess the meaning of the words you don’t know in Psalm 23, a very famous psalm.
The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.
He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters.
He restores my soul. He leads me in paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.
Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me; your rod and your staff, they comfort me.
You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies; you anoint my head with oil; my cup overflows.
Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life, and I shall dwell in the house of the Lord forever.
Now compare the psalms in English and in Portuguese.

Você conseguiu deduzir o significado de muitas palavras? Você pode aplicar essa estratégia de leitura a outros textos que você conheça em sua língua materna, não só da Bíblia, mas como de qualquer outro texto, como letras de músicas, poemas, ou até mesmo de livros completos! Pratique essa sua nova habilidade!
Há também Bíblias em português e inglês na mesma página. Você pode adquirir uma Bíblia dessas e criar esse hábito. Tenho certeza de que você vai aprender muitas palavras assim!

Observe, que para fazer a pergunta usamos a palavra “DOES” no começo da oração. Essa palavra é um verbo, chamado de verbo auxiliar (auxiliary verb) Mas auxiliar o que? O verbo auxiliar vem para auxiliar o verbo principal (main verb) da oração. Quando se usa o verbo auxiliar (auxiliary verb), o verbo principal (main verb) não precisa ser conjugado!
Observe que na pergunta “Does Daniel live in Babylon”, o verbo LIVE não precisou do S que usamos na forma afirmativa: Daniel lives in Babylon, exatamente porque existe o verbo auxiliar.
O verbo auxiliar DO é também o verbo FAZER:
Sendo assim, o verbo DO é tanto o auxiliary verb quanto o main verb. Por exemplo:

grammarNotes: In this lesson, we’ll learn to express FREQUENCY.
HOW OFTEN does Daniel pray? Do you remember?
In this lesson, you’ll learn some FREQUENCY EXPRESSIONS, but before that, we need some more vocabulary about periods of time.
The word “time” means "hora", "tempo" e "vez". In this case, it means “vez”, so three times means “três vezes”, etc.
There’s a special word for “one time” – it’s “once” – and “two times” is “twice”, so
Daniel prays three times A day
Daniel prays three times PER day.
Note: You also use the simple present to express frequency (habitual actions). You use these expressions at the end of the sentence.
Daniel prays three times a day.
